desk.headline: Revenue up 40.5% to R26.1bn on NKD deal; HEPS up 2.0% to 523.0c as finance costs bite; tough H2 expected
results: Revenue jumped 40.5% to R26.1bn, almost all from German value retailer NKD, bought for about R9.6bn and included from 31 March.
In Africa, retail sales rose 3.1%, ahead of a market up 1.2%, but same-store sales were flat; gross margin rose 0.6 points to 40.6%.
Operating profit rose 30.7% to about R2.8bn, but finance costs more than doubled to over R1bn on acquisition debt, so HEPS grew only 2.0%.
Interim dividend up 2.0% to 329.5c; net debt was R7.7bn.

guidance.summary: Mr Price expects trading to stay difficult for the rest of the year in both Africa and Europe, with any recovery gradual; cheaper NKD refinancing should help from the second half.

points: Management described South Africa as heavily promotional, with fuel, utility costs and weak jobs squeezing shoppers.
Durban port delays mean some festive stock may arrive up to two weeks late, though major stock is expected before Christmas.
NKD earns most of its profit in the first half; hot weather disrupted European seasonal trading.
Management said no further acquisitions are being considered and online sales fell short of target.
